outside writes, transient writes, shared Git and credential files are not isolated

Implementer notes (Claude Opus 5.5, the lead). Use them as context only; the judgment is yours.

Scope: spec `pose-review-readiness-before-seal` (R1–R6, decisions D1–D2, ADR `2026-11-23-review-readiness-before-seal` with residual limits L1–L2). It moves refusals that used to arrive after a full review round to the earliest point that has their inputs:
- R1/R2: a new seal of a spec bundle refuses the `undeclared-delivery` finding at error severity in the delivery index, and, when the plan has structural facts, a decision or assumption that reaches no requirement or constraint (`pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_seal_readiness.go`, called from `sealReviewBundle`).
- R3: `pose review draft-check` (`internal/cli/review_draft_check.go`, `internal/pose/review_draft_check.go`). The content part of the bundle-attestation validation was extracted unchanged into `attestationContentBlockers`, which both the conclusion preflight and the draft check call. The dispatch writes the bundle and the round's open findings to the run's private temporary directory and names it in `POSE_REVIEW_DRAFT_CONTEXT`.
- R4: brief template `review-brief/8` (the `/7` text and its golden digest are unchanged).
- R5/R6: `pose delegate` names an oversized note; a completed run nothing concluded prints its `pose review conclude` command.
Each requirement has a regression test that failed with its fix mutated out. The full `go test ./...` of `pose-mcp` passed.

Please check in particular that the extraction of `attestationContentBlockers` changed no behaviour of `validateBundleAttestationWith`, that the draft check cannot accept a draft the conclusion refuses for content, and that the seal refusal cannot block a bundle already sealed.

This brief is review-brief/8, so its last step asks you to run `pose review draft-check --draft -` on your own draft. Please do: it is also a live test of R3.

Draft format rules, enforced by the conclusion preflight:
- New findings use short unprefixed IDs (N1, N2, …). Round-prefixed IDs go only in `prior_findings`, and only for the findings the brief lists under "Findings to account for" (none in round 1), with exactly id, status and evidence.
- Structural-delta mappings go inside the criterion that answers them, with `basis` set to a requirement or a decision of this spec (R1–R6, D1, D2).
- A criterion scoped to a component cites evidence from that component only.

Sandbox limits: the checkout is sealed and read-only. Never run `pose assess` or any other command that writes inside it: a run that changes the sealed checkout fails. Never `cd`; keep the checkout root as the working directory. If building or a scratch copy is not possible, run the focused Go tests (`go test ./internal/pose ./internal/cli -run 'DraftCheck|SealReadiness|SealRefuses|DelegateNamesTheNoteLimit|Brief|SealedGate|OnlyTheSigning'`, `go vet`) and cite the sealed canonical result for the rest, stating the limit. A tool you cannot rerun in the sandbox is a limit of the run, not a defect of the subject: cite the sealed evidence that covers it, then decide on the code itself.
